completed_default_decision.reason: Retain Rafael Castor in both name consumers for source selector 00. Both B317 replies use that exact clean command. The initialized getter binds the name and a representative B317 replay still needs to verify its displayed speaker.

Retain approved Hodram and Joakim with Bergstrom. The two native forms intentionally differ by the middle component. Assistance against a common foe and tactical blame add no new rank or permanent alliance.
Retain approved Lil Argot and exact default-name macros. Her curious, flippant, compassionate and deliberately teasing replies do not invent kinship or romance.
Retain approved Maria Li and full Maria Huamei Li. The later B115 source explicitly uses actor3 within SC2; her moral argument and invitation establish no new rank, kinship or male identity.

Retain Janus Pasar, the established rendering of Jenasu Pasaa. Correct provisional Jenas references in contextual metadata; his injury and the tablet discussion do not establish a new personal relationship.
Retain Claudio Manaus. Rafael’s Clau and Claudio’s Rafi are supported familiar dialogue forms. Rumor, panic and flattery add no relationship beyond the exchange.
Retain Julio Erneco. His aged, reluctant speech does not justify Boss replacing the explicit Admiral address or an invented kinship with Lil or the priest.

Retain Cristina Erneco consistently with the bound current consumers for this scope. Correct provisional Christina references; wider earlier spelling consumers remain in the broader name review, without inventing a familial relationship from her surname.
Retain Arcadius Eudoxios and full Arcadius Eirene Eudoxios; B168 uses this original actor, not Fernando.

Retain approved Camille Overijssel and full Camille Marinus Overijssel, matching the clean components and established consumers. Lil addresses Camille by the approved given name; no relationship is invented.
Retain Xien Yan. His sharp B115 bandit rebuke belongs to the exact source actor10, not a substituted Lil companion or a newly ranked officer.

Retain Jam Ludwyan and full Jam Jack Ludwyan as the established source-bound forms. Use that exact letter signature; the provisional Ledoyen draft neither establishes a new spelling nor a historical French identity.
Retain Yukihisa Shiraki and full Yukihisa Genjo Shiraki. His contemplative and formal warrior speech needs no invented Lord title, family link or new rank.
Retain Cesare Tony, matching the clean components. His ornate figurehead admiration and private spiritual reflections do not make him a priest or introduce a different title.
Retain Emilio Ferog, matching the clean identity and native consumers. The bear scene explicitly names Emilio and reveals his real sleep while playing dead; he is distinct from Fernando.
Retain Angelo Puccini. Bianca is explicitly his sister and dead in the later confession; his reported fever encounter does not create a living replacement or a newly named ghost actor.
Retain Gerhard Adernkatz. His response to Noritsune is personal admiration and does not make him a member of the historical clan.
Retain Al Shin and full Al Ferid Shin. His decisive help to Aziza establishes no romance, marriage or ownership of her.

Retain Charles Rochefort and full Charles Jean Rochefort, faithful to the source components and established consumers. His hesitant unfinished objection in the dark cave adds no invented body part or biography.

Retain established Carlo Sinat in both consumers and reconcile the story introduction from Sinato/Cinato to Sinat. Merchant skills and grief do not supply a new scholarly title or warrant a speculative spelling.
Retain Fernando Dias. Clean actor20 owns the wall discovery, statue alarm, curse concern and bodily-heaviness replies in B251; these are not Lil speaking twice or an anonymous extra sailor.
Retain Ian Dukov, supported by イアン/ドゥーコフ. The vodka joke does not license added nationality or biography.
Retain Samwell Khan and full Samwell da Khan, preserving the reviewed component order and particle. His advice and warnings add no historical identity or family connection.
Retain Manuel Almeida. His sea/mother poem does not prove his mother died or supply a priest/poet title for the nameplate.

Retain Sera Shahrbaraz and full Sera Altos Shahrbaraz. B15’s embedded anonymous Foreign Girl label must remain unrevealing; B40’s named native actor and opaque cry do not justify translating her language.
Retain Yifa Sol. Martial-arts practice and reference to a personal teacher do not assign that teacher to Maria or supply an unsupported new rank.
Retain Julian Lopes for actor26. His chivalric intervention and dismay are not actor63 Julian Vermeer’s lines; a shared given name does not merge their identities.

Retain Aziza Nurennahar consistently with her full self-introduction. Just call me Aziza permits familiar address; her pirate father and the rescue establish no relationship with Al beyond the source exchange.
Retain James Clifford. His manipulation, insults and fire metaphor do not establish an actual fire injury or a new title.
Retain Martin Speyer. The Hanseatic cog identification and attack are scene context, not an invented shipowner title or historical identity.
Retain Pedro Valdes and full Pedro de Valdes as the reference identity mentioned by Maria and Escante. He is not a newly observed speaker; the explicit de component adds no invented nobility.
Retain Hardum Pasha and full Hardum Ahmet Pasha as the source-bound components. Pasha is used as the source’s address; do not invent Lord or a new biographical claim.
Retain Barbarossa Hayreddin and full Barbarossa Fazul Hayreddin. The carried-on Barbarossa name is explicit, but biological descent or a separate formal title is not.
Retain Fernan Silveira in both name consumers and the source surname Silveira in the trader’s account.
Retain Geronimo Espinosa and full Geronimo de Espinosa. Keep the already qualified de component; the challenge does not prove a new rank or nationality.
Retain Abraham Uddin and full Abraham Ibn Uddin. The source identifies him as with the Uddin Company; do not invent ownership, a new religious office or unsupported ethnicity from the name.

Retain registered Zamorin Nagarpur and full Zamorin Ahmad Nagarpur. Reconcile Nagalpur in dialogue to Nagarpur. Preserve native components without independently expanding Zamorin into a new rank or historical biography.
Retain Duarte Pereira and full Duarte Lopes de Pereira. Source dialogue itself supports both Governor and Admiral addresses in their respective lines.

Retain Antony Kuhn and full Antony von Kuhn. Correct Kuen in this dialogue to the registered identity. Do not silently identify the fictional character with an external historical Coen or infer nationality from a particle.
Retain Sojin Kurushima. The Ming/foreigner insult does not create a new employer title or a real-world identity in the name.
Retain Vasquez Maldonado and full Vasquez de Maldonado. His Caribbean-pirate claims and self-interested bargain do not justify a liberator or governor title.
Retain Diogo Escante and full Diogo de Escante. Conqueror is the source’s contextual address; independence rhetoric does not establish a lawful new crown or benevolent motive.
Retain Robert Stork for actor44 in the ambush. Preserve the separate source reference to Richard in B30 instead of silently renaming either actor to reconcile different passages.
Retain Gilberto Graus. His plantation-worker ownership claim and rough threats belong to the source antagonist, without adding an office or a completed death.
Retain Simon Linares, the established source-matching name of the officer ordering the attack on Portuguese rebels.
Retain Alonso Rosa and full Alonso de Rosa, preserving the source particle and the officer's formation order.
Retain Mushari Sidra and full Mushari Es Sidra. The withdrawal orders refer to his fleet; the source component Es is not expanded into an invented title or ancestry.
Retain Arnajud Jaume. Use the same Arnajud in the two-fleet order rather than the dialogue’s Al Najuud variant; do not invent a title or split one source component into unproved names.
Retain the registered Nagayoshi Kamuro surname correction. The source カムロ supports Kamuro; the iron-armored ships do not establish a historical warrior identity or a new office.
Retain Juan Blanco. His friendly reinforcement offer remains a distinct conditional speaker, not another name for Escante.
Retain Vels Granat and full Vels Wilhelm Granat, matching the source components of Gerhard's former pupil without inventing a new kinship.

Retain Jacks Bloom, faithful to Jakkusu Buruumu and both native consumers. The source explicitly calls him English; do not change him to a historical French Jacques or infer nationality from spelling.
Retain Julian Vermeer. His drinking and alleged betrayal supply no new occupation title, nationality or moral label in his nameplate.
Retain Yuris Huygens, the source-bound forms. Correct older Ulis/Huygen body spellings; noble birth does not establish a newly named hereditary title.
Retain Plett Perrault, consistently with the native consumers. Correct Prett Perrot in the earlier prose; the source murderer is brought alive and his fate is left to the client.
Retain Jean Ramusio. Reconcile Ramgio and independent provisional Ramzio to this installed identity. His French origin is explicit, while his self-praise remains character speech.
Retain Gabriel Cardocci as the existing source-bound rendering of ガブリエル/カルドッチ. Agreement violations and repeated encounters add no alternate person or historical identity.
Retain Jacob Portunto. An illicit trader’s piracy and cargo complaint do not justify a more specific smuggling conviction or new captain rank in the nameplate.
Retain Peralonso Aguirre, a sensible source-bound Spanish name. His spy role and comic overfamiliarity establish no historical identity or relationship with Lil.
Retain Zaganos Bey as the established full name. Bey is a source name component, not a new rank conferred by this review; capture does not prove execution.
Retain William Clive. English piracy is explicit; wild shrieks do not make him an animal, prove magic or support a mental-health diagnosis.
Retain Hernan Berio. Reconcile the independent provisional Berrio to Berio. Self-aggrandizing sama supports great in dialogue, not an invented Lord title.
Retain Iscal Yasar. The royal target and defeat sequence add no new rank, title or narrator-certified death to the name.
Retain Richard Townsend. English workers and defection are explicit story facts; FE monologue context alone does not prove a static speaker/portrait binding or an already received governorship.
Keep the established spelling. His familiarity and interest in the book remain in the dialogue.
Retain Mikhail Letzel and full Mikhail Volk Letzel, faithful to the source components and established consumers. His opportunistic cave joke and apology establish no romantic relationship with Lil.
Retain Sirwood Eme. The symbol-based foreign cry remains semantically opaque; Sirwood is a name component, not the English title Sir.
Retain Mivor Genz in both native consumers for ミヴォール/ゲンツ. Reconcile spoken Gentz to the existing legible Genz;the engagement and extravagant affection establish no noble rank or reciprocal romance.
Retain Sanghyeon Kan, matching サンヒョン/カン and both consumers; reconcile provisional Sang Hyeon to the installed given name. He is a senior fellow student, not a biological brother.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Paolo Centurione
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: パオロ / チェントリオネ
focused_retention_reviews.context: The original actor getter supplies this name. No exact static speech preamble for this actor was found in the four retail archives. The source identifies them without a dialogue assignment in this search.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep Paolo with Centurione. It matches the original name components and distinguishes his identity from Paulo Morais. The surname also matches the established Centurione Company.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Paolo preserves パオロ and Centurione agrees with the family name behind the Centurione Co. label. Keep the personal name in the actor field and the company name in the Forces roster.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Charles Gilban
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: チャールズ / ギルバン
focused_retention_reviews.context: The original actor getter supplies this name. No exact static speech preamble for this actor was found in the four retail archives. The source identifies them without a dialogue assignment in this search.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep the given name and the existing Latin spelling of ギルバン. The surname distinguishes this record from Charles Rochefort. No extra middle name appears in the Japanese fields.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Use Charles for チャールズ and retain the established Gilban for ギルバン. The family component distinguishes him from Charles Rochefort in the two default name forms.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Paulo Morais
focused_retention_reviews.context: The original actor getter supplies this name. No exact static speech preamble for this actor was found in the four retail archives. The source identifies them without a dialogue assignment in this search.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Retain Paulo for パウロ and Morais for モライス. The source distinguishes the given name from Paolo, and the existing Latin spelling gives both components without expanding either.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Enzo Regioni
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: エンツォ / レジオーニ
focused_retention_reviews.context: The original actor getter supplies this name. No exact static speech preamble for this actor was found in the four retail archives. The source identifies them without a dialogue assignment in this search.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep Enzo for エンツォ and the established Regioni for レジオーニ. Both consumers present the same personal name, with no additional source component.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Keep Enzo for エンツォ and the established Regioni for レジオーニ. The faction and the compact fleet template have their own fields.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Salid Ajar
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: サリド / アジャール
focused_retention_reviews.context: Rafael argues for passage through Hayreddin’s waters. Salid taunts him and objects when Hayreddin decides to let him pass.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep Salid, the name Hayreddin uses when telling him to wait. Ajar preserves the second source component. The scene supplies his allegiance without adding a formal rank to his nameplate.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Hayreddin addresses him as サリド while reining in his threats. Salid matches the form used in the exchange, while Ajar preserves the separate family component.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Ibn Niyadi
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: イブン / ニヤーディー
focused_retention_reviews.context: Uddin asks Rafael to consider an alliance overnight. Ibn Niyadi directs Rafael to the accommodations Uddin arranged. Uddin asks to hear Rafael’s decision. On acceptance, Ibn Niyadi acknowledges the order to show him into the reception room.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep both parts of the source name in their stored order. The short, courteous replies identify the same person at both of Uddin’s meetings and supply no title to append.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Retain Ibn and Niyadi as the two authored components. He shows Rafael the way after Uddin offers an alliance. The formal courtesy does not require a new title.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Jorge Albacete
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: ホルヘ / アルバセテ
focused_retention_reviews.context: Escante seeks Hodram’s help against Maldonado. Jorge objects to Hodram’s tone before Escante takes over.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep the two Spanish name components. The portrait label identifies the speaker of the single protective interjection while Escante and Hodram negotiate. It need not name an office or rank.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Retain both components of ホルヘ・アルバセテ. His sharp interjection during Escante’s introduction has the same name as the default catalogue entry.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Akaboo Damai
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: アカブー / ダーマイー
focused_retention_reviews.context: The original actor getter supplies this name. No exact static speech preamble for this actor was found in the four retail archives. The source identifies them without a dialogue assignment in this search.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep the project spelling for アカブー and ダーマイー in both getters. The two components identify one actor. The available source fields give no additional Latin form or title.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Keep the project’s phonetic Akaboo for アカブー and preserve the separate ダーマイー component as Damai. The current name is consistent with the earlier cooking pitch and the short fleet-name getter.

focused_retention_reviews.speaker: Charlotte Miller
focused_retention_reviews.source_meaning: シャルロット / ミレール
focused_retention_reviews.context: Charlotte questions Rafael’s plans for a village market, especially the labor, wages and materials. Rafael brings the promised wood. Charlotte thanks him and commits to building the market.
focused_retention_reviews.localization_note: Keep Charlotte, the name Rafael uses directly, and Miller for the separate source field. The market exchange establishes her practical role without turning it into a title or inventing a relationship.
focused_retention_reviews.previous_retention_note: Charlotte matches Rafael’s spoken address when he brings the timber. The default nameplate and catalogue retain ミレール as the established surname Miller.

SC0 B37.summary: Rafael argues for passage through Hayreddin’s waters. Salid taunts him and objects when Hayreddin decides to let him pass.

speeches.Japanese:
FI提督
どうします？
speeches.English: Admiral FI, what should we do?

speeches.Japanese:
フリオさん、アルジェ海賊って
スペインと仲が悪いって
聞いたんだけど…
speeches.English:
Julio, I heard the Algiers pirates 
 and Spain don't get along...

speeches.Japanese:
スペイン船を中心につけ狙って
おるからの。王立海軍の司令官である
バルデス提督とは近々
衝突することになるじゃろうな
speeches.English:
They prey chiefly on Spanish ships.
 I expect they'll clash with Admiral
 Valdes, commander of the royal 
 navy, before long.

speeches.Japanese:
スペインの圧力のおかげで
最近はポルトガルの艦隊が
商売しにくくなったって話だし…
speeches.English:
And I've heard Spanish pressure
 has been making it harder
 for Portuguese fleets
 to trade lately...

speeches.Japanese:
この際、同じ敵を持つ者同士ってことで
何とかならないかな？
ほら、敵の敵は味方っていうじゃない？
speeches.English:
Could a shared enemy help us?
 The enemy of my enemy...

speeches.Japanese:
かーっ。まったく、おめえはよー
甘えっつーの
相手は海賊だぜ？
speeches.English:
You're too trusting. 
 They're pirates!

speeches.Japanese: いやはや。まずいですねえ…
speeches.English: This is bad...

speeches.Japanese:
貴様ら！
この南地中海で
何をやっている！！
speeches.English:
You there! What are you doing
 in the southern Mediterranean?!

speeches.Japanese: げ！　見つかったか！
speeches.English: Ugh! They've spotted us!

speeches.Japanese: さて、どうやって切り抜けますか
speeches.English: How do we escape?

speeches.Japanese:
奴は、『誇りを重んずる男』と聞く
逃げ腰な態度は、かえって餌食に
なるかもしれん。ここは堂々として
おったほうがよいじゃろうな
speeches.English:
I hear he's a proud man. Looking 
 ready to run may only make us
 easier prey. Best to stand tall.

speeches.Japanese:
堂々とした態度…？
…よーし
おほん
speeches.English: Stand tall...? All right. Ahem.

speeches.Japanese:
えー、我々は…！
『打倒スペイン、ポルトガル復興』を旗印に
世界を翔るポルトガルの…
speeches.English:
We are... Portuguese voyagers
 sailing the world under
 the banner of defeating Spain
 and restoring Portugal...

speeches.Japanese: FOだ！
speeches.English: FO!

speeches.Japanese:
そして私が
FU提督だ！
speeches.English: And I'm Admiral FU!

speeches.Japanese: おお！　立派なもんじゃ
speeches.English: Oh! Splendid.

speeches.Japanese: やんや、やんや。（ぱちぱちぱち）
speeches.English: Hear, hear! (applause)

speeches.Japanese:
バァカか？　貴様っ！
皆殺しだっ！！
speeches.English:
Are you an idiot?! We'll kill
 you all!!

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、ダメか…
やられるっ…
speeches.English: No good... We're dead...

speeches.Japanese: まあ、待て。サリド
speeches.English: Wait, Salid.

speeches.Japanese:
貴様ら、打倒スペインとか
ぬかしおったな
speeches.English: You said 'defeat Spain,' yes?

speeches.Japanese: そ、そうだ
speeches.English: Y-yes.

speeches.Japanese:
はははは、面白い！
無敵艦隊を敵に回すというのか？
ふはははは！
speeches.English:
Ha ha ha! How entertaining!
 You mean to take on
 the Spanish Armada? Ha ha ha!

speeches.Japanese: な、何がおかしいんだ！
speeches.English: W-what's funny?!

speeches.Japanese: …貴様は口に気を付けたほうがいいな
speeches.English: ...Watch your tongue.

speeches.Japanese:
クラウ！　ここは
FIに任せて
さ、総帥の腕の見せ所ですよ
がんばってください
speeches.English:
Clau! Leave this to FI. Come 
 now, this is your chance to show 
 what our leader can do. Good luck!

speeches.Japanese:
むむ…、ちっ。じゃあ
FI、がんばれ
speeches.English: Tch. All right. FI, good luck.

speeches.Japanese:
よし、いちかばちかだ
…やってみよう
speeches.English: All or nothing... Let's try.

speeches.Japanese:
おいおい。さっきの勢いは、どうした？
無敵艦隊に勝とうと思ってんなら
俺たちと張り合うくらいの心構えは
あるだろうが！
speeches.English:
Hey, where'd all that bravado go?
 If you mean to beat the Armada,
 you must at least be ready to stand
 against us!

speeches.Japanese: そ、その通りだ！
speeches.English: Exactly!

speeches.Japanese:
ほう。大きく出たな
だが、今の貴様では命取りになろう
speeches.English:
Quite a bold claim. But try
 it as you are now, and it'll get 
 you killed.

speeches.Japanese: そうだ！　今はその時ではない！！
speeches.English: Right! Now is not the time!

speeches.Japanese: 何だと？
speeches.English: What?!

speeches.Japanese:
ふははは
では、いつがその時なのだ？
speeches.English: Hahaha. Then when?

speeches.Japanese:
だから…経験を積み、鍛えるのだ！
そして、あなたとも対等に渡り合える
実力を身につける！
speeches.English:
We'll gain experience and train, 
 until we can face you as equals!

speeches.Japanese:
わははは！
みすみす他人がのし上がるのを
だまって見ているお人好しが、どこに
いるんだ！
speeches.English:
Ha ha ha! Who'd be fool enough 
 to stand by and let someone else 
 rise to power?

speeches.Japanese:
アルジェ海賊は、噂に聞いたよりも
臆病だな？　我々が強くなると
勝てないとでも？
speeches.English:
The Algiers pirates are more 
 timid than I'd heard. Afraid 
 you won't be able to beat us once
 we're stronger?

speeches.Japanese: なぁにぃ！？
speeches.English: What?!

speeches.Japanese:
では、ここを自由に行き来させて
いただきたい！　いずれは
スペインの無敵艦隊を倒してみせる！
speeches.English:
Then let us travel freely through
 these waters! One day, we'll defeat
 the Spanish Armada!

speeches.Japanese:
てめえっ！
図に乗るにもほどがあるぞ！！
speeches.English:
You little...! Don't push
 your luck!!

speeches.Japanese:
貴様……
FIとか
名乗りおったな
speeches.English: You... called yourself FI?

speeches.Japanese:
ふはははは、面白い！
実に面白いぞ、若造！
speeches.English: Hahaha! Amusing. Very amusing, boy!

speeches.Japanese: 提督！！
speeches.English: Sir!!

speeches.Japanese:
よし。いいだろう。探検なり商売なり
して、その言葉に恥じぬ力を手に
入れるがよい。その時は胸を貸して
やろう
speeches.English:
Very well. Explore, trade, and gain
 the strength to live up
 to those words. When you're ready, 
 I'll take you on.

speeches.Japanese: ハイレディン提督！
speeches.English: Admiral Hayreddin!

speeches.Japanese:
俺に、こんなひよっ子を本気で
相手にしろと言うのか？
speeches.English:
Do you expect me to take fledglings
 like these seriously?

speeches.Japanese:
え？
あ、いや…
speeches.English: Huh? Uh...

speeches.Japanese:
構わん
たまにはこういう遊びも面白かろう
speeches.English: No matter. Such games amuse me.

speeches.Japanese:
…はっ
分かりました
speeches.English: Yes. Understood.

speeches.Japanese:
よし。貴様らは、地中海を往来する
ことを認めてやる。ただし、商売は
他の海域でやれ
speeches.English:
You may cross the Mediterranean. 
 But trade elsewhere.

speeches.Japanese: な、何だと？
speeches.English: W-what?

speeches.Japanese:
スペインのバルデスとオスマン＝トルコ
この２大勢力を怒らせて、今の貴様らの
手に負えると思うのか？　ヤツらは
この俺ほど甘くはないぞ
speeches.English:
Do you think you can handle
 angering both Valdes of Spain
 and the Ottoman Turks? Neither 
 is as forgiving as I am.

speeches.Japanese:
地中海で覇を唱えたいなら
まずは外で名を売ってからにしろ
よけいなもめ事は目障りだ
speeches.English:
If you aspire to rule
 the Mediterranean, make
 a name for yourselves
 elsewhere first. 
 I have no patience 
 for needless trouble.

speeches.Japanese: そうだな…。それと…
speeches.English: Let's see... One more thing...

speeches.Japanese: な、何か？
speeches.English: W-what?

speeches.Japanese:
スペイン船に襲われた時
この我らの海域でのみ
俺の船団が加勢してやる
speeches.English:
If Spanish ships attack you, 
 my fleet will come to your aid.
 But only in our waters.

speeches.Japanese: ええっ！　本当に！？
speeches.English: Really?!

speeches.Japanese:
必ずというわけにはいかんが
俺もこれでいて多忙な身だからな
speeches.English:
Don't count on it every time.
 I'm a busy man, you know.

speeches.Japanese: あ、ありがたいっ！！
speeches.English: T-thank you!!

speeches.Japanese:
もちろん、ハイレディン一家の縄張りに
手を出したりしたら、それは俺への
挑戦と受け取ろう。容赦はせんぞ
speeches.English:
Of course, encroach on 
 our territory and I'll take
 it as a challenge. I'll show 
 no mercy.

speeches.Japanese: も…もちろんだ！
speeches.English: O-of course!

speeches.Japanese: ふん。もしや貴様なら…
speeches.English: Hmph. Perhaps you...

speeches.Japanese:
いや、何でもない…。いいか
俺を楽しませるほど成長することだ
重々、約束は守ってもらうぞ
speeches.English:
No, nothing. Grow strong enough
 to entertain me, and keep
 your promise.

speeches.Japanese: …分かった。約束しよう
speeches.English: ...I understand. You have my word.

speeches.Japanese:
よし。いいだろう
皆の者、引き上げるぞ
speeches.English: Good. Everyone, withdraw.

speeches.Japanese: おう！
speeches.English: Aye!

speeches.Japanese:
なかなかハッタリもきいてたぜ！
やるじゃねーか
FI
speeches.English: That bluff worked! Not bad, FI!

speeches.Japanese: すごい約束を取り付けましたね
speeches.English: That's quite a promise you secured.

speeches.Japanese:
ふう…
自分でも驚いた
今になって怖くなってきたよ
speeches.English:
Whew... I surprised myself. Now
 that it's over, I'm starting 
 to feel scared.

speeches.Japanese:
へへっ、おめえみたいなやつが
“本番に強いタイプ”っていうのかもな
speeches.English: Heh. Maybe pressure suits you.

speeches.Japanese: あっぱれじゃな
speeches.English: Splendid.

speeches.Japanese:
みんなありがとう
でも、ああ言っちゃった手前
がんばって強くならないと
speeches.English:
Thanks, everyone. But after all
 that talk, I'd better work hard
 and get stronger.

SC0 B65.summary: Charlotte questions Rafael’s plans for a village market, especially the labor, wages and materials.

speeches.Japanese: …はい、これが今回の分よ
speeches.English:
...Here you are. 
 This is the latest batch.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう
ところで…ねえ、シャルロット
speeches.English: Thank you. By the way, Charlotte...

speeches.Japanese: なあに？
speeches.English: What?

speeches.Japanese:
やっぱり、商売をするなら
ちゃんとした交易所を建てたほうが
いいと思うんだ
speeches.English:
If you're going to trade here, 
 I think you ought to build a proper
 trading post.

speeches.Japanese: 交易所？
speeches.English: A trading post?

speeches.Japanese:
もっと多くの品目を扱って
専門に売買できるようにするんだ
speeches.English:
You could handle more kinds
 of goods and have a place just 
 for buying and selling.

speeches.Japanese:
そうすれば、交易のために
遠回りしてでもここに訪れる船が
出てくるよ
speeches.English:
Then ships would 
 go out of their way to trade here.

speeches.Japanese:
でも…、ちゃんとした交易所なら
そこで働く人も必要でしょ
村の人たちは、今の仕事で手一杯よ
speeches.English:
But who's going to run 
 the trading post? Everyone 
 in the village already 
 has their hands full.

speeches.Japanese:
人を雇えばいいのさ
交易所ができれば船が来るし
この街で働こうって人も
やって来るよ
speeches.English:
You could hire people. 
 A trading post would bring ships 
 here, and people looking for work
 would come, too.

speeches.Japanese:
どうやって、その人たちの
賃金を払うの？
speeches.English: How would we pay their wages?

speeches.Japanese:
交易所で商人に商業投資を募るのさ
最初にお金が入ってくれば
あとは交易の利益でやっていける
speeches.English:
You could ask merchants to invest
 in the post. Once you had the money
 to get started, the profits
 from trading could keep it going.

speeches.Japanese:
そんなにうまく行くかしら？
この村には、商人たちがわざわざ
交易所で取引するほどの
特産品がないわ
speeches.English:
Would that really work? What 
 do we make here that's worth 
 a merchant stopping to buy?

speeches.Japanese:
投資で村が発展すれば、もっと
たくさんの特産品を作れるように
なるんだ。新しい特産品だって
できる！
speeches.English:
Investment would help the village
 grow. You could produce more local 
 goods, and even develop new ones!

speeches.Japanese:
…投資してくれる人なんて
いるのかしら？
speeches.English: Would anyone really invest here?

speeches.Japanese: もちろん！　僕がするよ！
speeches.English: Of course! I'll invest.

speeches.Japanese:
…
やっぱり無理よ
speeches.English: No... I still don't think we can.

speeches.Japanese: どうして？
speeches.English: Why not?

speeches.Japanese:
この辺には、建築用の石材や木材が
ほとんどないの。大きな
交易所なんて建てられないわ
speeches.English:
There's hardly any building stone
 or timber around here. We couldn't 
 build a big trading post.

speeches.Japanese:
そんなの、運んでくればいいんだよ！
僕が木材を用意するから
心配しないで待ってて！
speeches.English:
Then we can bring it in! I'll get
 the timber. Don't worry. Just
 wait for me!

SC0 B66.summary: Rafael brings the promised wood. Charlotte thanks him and commits to building the market.

speeches.Japanese: FI…！

やあ、シャルロット！
木材を仕入れてきたよ！
これで、交易所を建てよう！
speeches.English:
Hi, Charlotte! I've brought
 the timber! Let's build
 that trading post!

speeches.Japanese:
すごい…！
でも…、こんなにたくさんの木材を
買えるだけのお金は村にないわ
speeches.English:
That's amazing! But the village
 can't afford all this timber.

speeches.Japanese: お金なんていらないよ
speeches.English: You don't have to pay me.

speeches.Japanese: そんな！
speeches.English: But...!

speeches.Japanese:
これも投資のうちなんだ
この村で特産品がたくさん買える
ようになったら
僕が真っ先に買いに来るからね！
speeches.English:
It's part of my investment. Once 
 you've got plenty of local goods 
 to sell, I'll be the first to come 
 and buy them!

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう、FI！
…時間はかかると思うけど、がんばって
きっと立派な交易所にするわね！
speeches.English:
Thank you, FI! It may 
 take a while, but I'll do my best
 to make it a trading post
 we can be proud of!

speeches.Japanese: 待ってるよ！
speeches.English: Can't wait!

speeches.Japanese:
さあ、忙しくなるわ！
がんばらなくちゃ！
speeches.English:
We'll have our hands full now! I'd 
 better get to work.

SC0 B147.summary: Uddin asks Rafael to consider an alliance overnight. Ibn Niyadi directs Rafael to the accommodations Uddin arranged.

speeches.Japanese: ！　うわあ…。す、すごい…！
speeches.English: W-wow... Amazing...!

speeches.Japanese:
驚かせてしまってすまないね
FI君、いや
FO総帥と
呼ばせてもらおうか
speeches.English:
Forgive me for startling 
 you, FI... 
 or perhaps I should call 
 you FO's leader.

speeches.Japanese:
ウッディーンさん…
いえ、総帥…
speeches.English: Mr. Uddin... I mean, sir...

speeches.Japanese: 早速用件から入らせてもらうよ
speeches.English: I shall come straight to the point.

speeches.Japanese: は、はい
speeches.English: Y-yes.

speeches.Japanese: 我々と協定同盟してはくれまいか
speeches.English:
Would you consider forming 
 an alliance with us?

speeches.Japanese: 協定…
speeches.English: Pact?

speeches.Japanese:
まあ、怪しむのも無理はない
いきなりな上に、ぶしつけなのは
こちらも十分承知しているつもりだ
speeches.English:
I understand your suspicion. I am
 well aware that this is a sudden 
 and rather forward request.

speeches.Japanese:
無論、協定依頼は勢力の重要事項だ
簡単に決断できることでは
ないだろう…
speeches.English:
An alliance is a serious matter. No
 easy choice, surely...

speeches.Japanese:
まあ、怪しむのも無理はない
君たちがアフリカでどんな目に
あったかぐらいはもちろん
調べてある
speeches.English:
I understand your suspicion. 
 Naturally, I have looked into what 
 happened to you in Africa.

speeches.Japanese:
協定依頼に敏感になるわけも分かる
だが、そこをあえて頼んでいるのだ
speeches.English:
I know why an offer like 
 this would trouble you. Even 
 so, I am asking you to consider it.

speeches.Japanese:
即答は求めんよ。一晩考えてみてくれ
用件は以上だ。宿のほうはこちらで
用意してある
さ、行きたまえ
speeches.English:
No answer is needed tonight. Think 
 it over. Rooms are ready.
 That is all. Go and rest.

speeches.Japanese: こちらです
speeches.English: This way.

speeches.Japanese: …ありがとう
speeches.English: Thanks...

SC0 B148.summary: Uddin asks to hear Rafael’s decision. On acceptance, Ibn Niyadi acknowledges the order to show him into the reception room.

speeches.Japanese: 決めてくれたかな
speeches.English: Have you decided?

speeches.Japanese:
はい
いろいろと考えましたが…
speeches.English: Yes. After much thought...

speeches.Japanese: ふむ。聞かせてもらおう
speeches.English: Hmm. Let us hear it.

speeches.Japanese:
あなたを信頼します
これからよろしくお願いします
speeches.English:
You have my trust. Let us
 work together.

speeches.Japanese:
そう言ってくれてうれしいよ。それでは
FA総帥
早速、商談に入りたいのだが
よろしいかな？
speeches.English:
Glad to hear it. Mr. FA, 
 shall we discuss business?

speeches.Japanese: は、はい。分かりました
speeches.English: Y-yes. Understood.

speeches.Japanese:
では、別室へ案内させよう
…
FA総帥を
応接室にお通ししてくれ
speeches.English:
I'll have you shown to another 
 room. ...Please show Mr. FA
 to the reception room.

speeches.Japanese: かしこまりました
speeches.English: At once.

speeches.Japanese:
まず、協定の内容だが
目標はザモリン・ナガルプル侯
インド周辺に勢力を持っている
speeches.English:
First, the purpose of our alliance.
 Our target is Lord 
 Zamorin Nagalpur, who holds power
 around India.

speeches.Japanese:
金の亡者といった男でね
品位のない彼の強欲な商法のおかげで
我々は大いに迷惑している
speeches.English:
The man worships money.
 His grasping, undignified
 business practices have caused us
 considerable trouble.

speeches.Japanese:
彼が所有する商会の財力は大きく
その力は侮れないが、おせじにも
“人物”とは言いがたい男だ
speeches.English:
The company has vast wealth. 
 That power is formidable, but its
 master lacks virtue.

speeches.Japanese:
我らが組めば
いずれ倒すことができよう
speeches.English:
Together, we should be able
 to defeat him in time.

speeches.Japanese: はい
speeches.English: Yes.

speeches.Japanese:
そこでだ
君が不安になるところだとは思うが…
speeches.English: Now the part that may concern you...

speeches.Japanese: ナガルプル商会を倒した後のことですね
speeches.English: What happens after Nagalpur falls?

speeches.Japanese:
その通り。さすがだね。協定自体は
そこで終了だ。契約の書面が
あるわけでもないのだが、あとは
『不可侵条約』に切り替えてもらいたい
speeches.English:
Precisely. Our alliance will end 
 there. We have no written contract,
 but afterward I would like us
 to agree to a nonaggression pact.

speeches.Japanese: 不可侵…ですか
speeches.English: A nonaggression pact...?

speeches.Japanese:
私の本拠であるアラブ周辺においては
ある程度の比率で君の商会と共存
できよう。その他の都市、港は
君の自由裁量に任せる
speeches.English:
My company is based in Arabia. 
 We can share those markets, within 
 reason. In other cities and ports, 
 you may act as you see fit.

speeches.Japanese:
アラブ圏に、あまり手を出すな
ということですね
speeches.English: So go easy on the Arabian markets.

speeches.Japanese:
そういうことだ
我々も決して君たちの邪魔はしないと
約束しよう
speeches.English:
Correct. We promise never
 to obstruct you.

speeches.Japanese:
ウッディーンにマスカットの
シェアを分けてもらいました
speeches.English:
Uddin shared his Muscat
 market share with you.

speeches.Japanese:
ウッディーンにソコトラの
シェアを分けてもらいました
speeches.English:
Uddin granted you some 
 of his market share in Socotra.

speeches.Japanese:
分かりました
他にありますか？
speeches.English: Understood. Anything else?

speeches.Japanese:
いや、それだけでいい
手間をとらせてすまなかった
speeches.English:
No, that is all. Forgive me
 for taking up your time.

speeches.Japanese:
こちらこそ
まだまだ小さな
FOですが
協力させていただきます
speeches.English:
Not at all. FO may still 
 be small, but we'll do our part.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう
期待しているよ
speeches.English: Thank you. I look forward to it.

speeches.Japanese: では、ナガルプルを倒しましょう！
speeches.English: Then let's defeat Nagalpur!

speeches.Japanese:
うむ
互いに力を合わせ邁進しよう
speeches.English:
Yes. Let us join forces
 and press onward.

speeches.Japanese: 同盟は受けない、と？
speeches.English: You decline?

speeches.Japanese: 申し訳ありません…
speeches.English: My apologies...

speeches.Japanese:
アフリカの傷は癒えていない
というわけか
speeches.English: The wounds of Africa remain, then?

speeches.Japanese: いえ、そういうことでは…
speeches.English: No, that is not...

speeches.Japanese:
君ほどの者が判断したのだ。これよりは
敵同士、互いにインド洋の覇者を
めざそう。…というのは変かな？
speeches.English:
A man of your ability has made 
 his choice. Then let us
 be enemies, each striving
 for supremacy in the Indian Ocean. 
 ...Does that sound strange?

speeches.Japanese:
は、はい
…お手柔らかに
speeches.English: Y-yes... Go easy on us, won't you?

speeches.Japanese: ではさらばだ
speeches.English: Goodbye.

SC1 B140.summary: Escante seeks Hodram’s help against Maldonado. Jorge objects to Hodram’s tone before Escante takes over.

speeches.Japanese: やあ、あんたに紹介したい人がいる
speeches.English:
There's someone I'd like 
 you to meet.

speeches.Japanese:
メキシコの総督
ディオゴ・デ・エスカンテ様だ
speeches.English: Mexico's governor, Diogo de Escante.

speeches.Japanese: よろしく
speeches.English: Hello.

speeches.Japanese:
ほう…。その総督自らが
俺に何の用だ？
speeches.English:
The governor himself?
 What do you want with me?

speeches.Japanese:
てめえ、口のきき方に
気を付けやがれ！
speeches.English: Watch your mouth!

speeches.Japanese:
まあよい
君たちに相談したいことがあるのだ
speeches.English:
It's quite all right.
 I'd like a word with you.

speeches.Japanese: 俺に？
speeches.English: Me?

speeches.Japanese:
君はバスケス・デ・マルドナード
という男を知っているか？
speeches.English: Do you know Vasquez de Maldonado?

speeches.Japanese: …ああ
speeches.English: Yes.

speeches.Japanese:
我々は、ヤツにほとほと
手を焼いている
speeches.English: He has caused us endless trouble.

speeches.Japanese:
…あんたと同じスペイン国籍だったと
思うが？
speeches.English: But isn't he Spanish, like you?

speeches.Japanese:
彼の名目は、空席となった
キューバ総督の代行だが、その実態は
カリブ海一帯をおさえる海賊の
元締めのような男だ
speeches.English:
Officially, he's acting
 governor of Cuba 
 until the vacant 
 post is filled.
 In practice, he's the head 
 of the pirates controlling 
 the Caribbean.

speeches.Japanese:
本国と新大陸を行き来する我々の
商船を配下の海賊どもに次々と襲わせて
おいて、素知らぬ顔でリベートを
吸い上げ、私腹を肥やしている
speeches.English:
He has his pirates attack
 our merchant ships 
 sailing between Spain
 and the New World. 
 Then he pretends to know nothing 
 while pocketing his cut.

speeches.Japanese:
あのハイエナのような男を
早く排除せんと、この海域の
スペイン領の経営は崩壊してしまう
そんなことになったら…
speeches.English:
Unless that hyena is removed 
 soon, Spanish rule 
 in these waters will collapse. 
 And if that happens...

speeches.Japanese:
最近姿を現しはじめたイギリス人
どもに、カリブ海はおろか新大陸全域を
乗っ取られ、スペイン王国の屋台骨
そのものが揺らぐことにもなりかねん
speeches.English:
The English have begun to appear 
 here. They could seize 
 not just the Caribbean,
 but the entire New World.
 It could shake Spain 
 to its foundations.

speeches.Japanese:
そこで君たちと力をあわせて、ともに
あの逆賊を打ち倒したいという
わけなのだ。どうだろうか？
speeches.English:
Join us in defeating the traitor.
 What say you?

speeches.Japanese:
今の話が本当なら、彼は立派な
国家反逆罪だ
俺たちの出る幕でもなかろう
speeches.English:
If that's true, he's guilty of high
 treason. Surely you don't need us
 to deal with him.

speeches.Japanese:
明確な証拠がないゆえ、現状では
彼を断罪できない
スペインの同胞に対して、我々から
戦いを仕掛けるわけにもいかん
speeches.English:
We have no conclusive evidence 
 to condemn him. And we cannot
 simply attack a fellow Spaniard.

speeches.Japanese:
我々の代わりに君たちがマルドナードを
駆逐してくれるのであれば
協力は惜しまない
speeches.English:
Drive Maldonado out for us,
 and you will have our full support.

speeches.Japanese:
その結果、俺たちがカリブ海を制圧する
ことになっても構わないと？
speeches.English:
Even if we end up controlling
 the Caribbean?

speeches.Japanese:
輸送船に無差別攻撃を仕掛けるような
男がのさばっているよりは
我々に友好的な勢力がとりしきって
いてくれたほうが、百倍望ましい
speeches.English:
I'd much rather have a friendly
 power in charge than a man 
 who attacks transport
 ships indiscriminately.

speeches.Japanese:
ふっ。イギリスが来るのは困るが
俺たちであればくみしやすいという
ことか
speeches.English:
Heh. You don't want the English
 here, but you think we'll be easier
 to handle.

speeches.Japanese:
…そう、勘ぐらんでもらいたい
ものだな
speeches.English: Do not be so suspicious.

speeches.Japanese:
イギリスと本国とは全面的な交戦状態に
ある。おおっぴらにイギリスと
組むことはできん
speeches.English:
Spain is at war with England.
 We cannot openly join the English.

speeches.Japanese:
俺たちも、スペイン王が殺したいほど
憎んでいる新教徒だが？
speeches.English:
We're Protestants your king
 would gladly kill.

speeches.Japanese:
宗教戦争は、ヨーロッパでやって
くれればいい。私としては新大陸にまで
そんな無意味な対立を持ち込む気は
毛頭ない。しかし、イギリスは違う！
speeches.English:
Keep Europe's religious wars there.
 Such useless conflict has no place 
 here. England is different!

speeches.Japanese:
ヤツらは特別…、スペイン国民の
不倶戴天の敵だ！　この海域にイギリス
王国の国旗がたなびく光景など、想像
するだけでもおぞましいことだよ！
speeches.English:
The English are Spain's sworn
 enemies! The very thought
 of their flag flying over
 these waters disgusts me!

speeches.Japanese:
君たちにとっても損な話ではないと
思うが…。カリブ海進出を狙うので
あれば、マルドナードを相手にしない
わけにもいくまい
speeches.English:
This benefits you as well. If you
 mean to expand into the Caribbean, 
 you'll have to face Maldonado
 sooner or later.

speeches.Japanese:
彼も、海賊あがりの豪腕提督だ
今でも現役で、強力な船団を率いて
いる。君たちの力だけでは
もてあますだろう
speeches.English:
He is a powerful admiral and former
 pirate, still leading a strong 
 fleet. Alone, you may struggle.

speeches.Japanese:
…理屈は分かった
こちらとしても、力を蓄える好機…
speeches.English:
...I see your reasoning. 
 It would give us a chance to build 
 our strength...

speeches.Japanese:
（…こちらとしても、スペイン領の
　分裂につけこんで、力を蓄える
　好機です。両者を敵にまわすのは
　得策ではありません。）
speeches.English:
(This split in Spain's colonies
 is our chance to gain strength.
 Making both sides enemies
 would be unwise.)

speeches.Japanese: ふむ…
speeches.English: Hm...

speeches.Japanese:
いいだろう
その話、乗ってみることにする
speeches.English: Very well. We'll accept.

speeches.Japanese:
君が、物分かりの悪い人物でなくて
安心したよ
speeches.English: Glad you are reasonable.
